Day-2 operations for a Deploy App instance on the Kubernetes platform (pvarki/opendefence-platform, alpha): redeploying, managing secrets, rotating certificates/CA, the database, upgrades, and teardown. This stack uses Kubernetes-native operators rather than the legacy miniwerk/CFSSL pieces. For initial standup see Deploy on Kubernetes; for failure modes see Troubleshooting & teardown.

Redeploy / apply changes

The canonical interface is task. To re-apply the full phased stack to the current cluster:

task deploy          # phased apply of infra + apps with readiness gates
task deploy:local    # local (kind) overlays explicitly
task deploy:cloud    # cloud overlays against the k3s VM kubeconfig

task deploy re-renders the phased kustomizations and applies them with kubectl apply --server-side, waiting for each phase's controllers (cloudnative-pg, cert-manager, external-secrets-operator, then trust-manager) before applying the next. Do not run ad-hoc multi-phase kubectl apply that skips these rollout waits.

To apply a single service after editing its manifests, build its overlay and apply it (use --enable-helm for any kustomization that includes Helm charts):

kubectl kustomize --enable-helm k8s/<service>/overlays/local | \
  kubectl apply --server-side -f -

Keep base/ environment-agnostic and put environment-specific changes (images, ingress routes, certificates, hostnames) in overlays/<env>/. When you change deployment phases or kustomization paths, keep taskfile.yaml in sync.

Secrets (external-secrets-operator)

Secrets are managed by the external-secrets-operator, which is deployed in infra-phase1 and gated on before later phases. Runtime secrets for the core API surface as the opendefense-rmapi-runtime-secrets Secret in opendefense-system, materialized from the operator's ExternalSecret definitions (k8s/opendefense-system/base/resources/opendefense-secrets.external-secrets.yaml). To rotate or change a secret, update the backing secret store / ExternalSecret rather than editing the Kubernetes Secret by hand, then let the operator re-sync.

Not yet documented. The backing secret store used per environment (the cluster SecretStore/ClusterSecretStore provider) and the end-to-end steps to rotate a credential are still to be written here.

Certificate and CA rotation (cert-manager + opendefense-pki)

There is no CFSSL here. The CA chain is defined in k8s/opendefense-pki/ (CA cert, CA issuer, OpenDefense CA, intermediate CA, and the trust bundle), cert-manager issues from it, and trust-manager distributes the trust bundle cluster-wide. The core API issues client/service certs through cert-manager using the intermediate CA issuer:

Leaf certificates are renewed by cert-manager on its normal schedule. Rotating the CA/intermediate is a opendefense-pki change, re-applied through infra-phase2 (which waits for trust-manager) so the updated trust bundle propagates.

Not yet documented. A safe CA-rotation runbook — issue a new intermediate, roll the trust bundle via trust-manager, re-issue leaf certs — and its user-impact window are still to be written. Rotating the CA affects mTLS for every enrolled device, so do not attempt it from this page until the runbook exists.

Database (cloudnative-pg)

PostgreSQL is managed by the cloudnative-pg operator (deployed in infra-phase1; the deploy flow waits for deployment/cnpg-controller-manager in cnpg-system). The core API's database is a CNPG cluster whose app credentials are exposed as the opendefense-rmapi-postgres-app secret. Use CNPG's own mechanisms (Cluster resource, backups, scheduled backups) for DB operations rather than touching the pods directly.

Not yet documented. Whether CNPG scheduled backups / object-store backup is configured per environment, and the matching restore procedure, are still to be written here.

Upgrades

Upgrade by changing the pinned images in the relevant overlays/<env>/ (and operator/tool versions in mise.toml), then re-running task deploy so the phased rollout with readiness gates applies the change. As on the legacy stack, the model favors redeploying over long-lived in-place maintenance. For cloud, rebuild and redeploy the Zarf package (task zarf:package:cloud, then zarf package deploy ... --set OPENDEFENSE_HOST=...) — see Deploy on Kubernetes.

Teardown

Local (kind) — destroys the whole cluster and all instance data:
task down            # alias of cluster:delete (kind delete cluster --name opendefense-kind)
On a shared/cloud cluster you typically remove the workload by deleting its namespace instead of deleting the cluster (still destructive to that instance's data):
kubectl delete namespace opendefense-system

See Troubleshooting & teardown for the full teardown discussion and the legacy down -v equivalence.

Monitoring

The platform deploys its own monitoring phase (Grafana, Loki, Alloy, Prometheus). Use it for logs and metrics; see Audit logging & observability for the audit-log model and what to watch. Organization-wide conventions are deferred to the Community & Standards page (in Contribute to Project).
